reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) concerns HEA coatings on Q235, not thermal oxidation to form magnetite, and provides no support for any of the key premises about Fe3O4 formation, barrier properties, or native oxide behavior.
premises: Thermal oxidation of Q235 steel in air at ~220°C forms a continuous, adherent magnetite (Fe3O4) layer
A uniform Fe3O4 film acts as a physical and electrochemical barrier to Cl⁻ and O₂ ingress
This barrier reduces electron transfer and suppresses localized pitting initiation
Untreated Q235 steel has an uneven, thinner native oxide that permits localized breakdown
The protective effect is effective in 3.5 wt.% NaCl at 25°C and 80°C
